{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nc-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"ca9817ff018c089d14241b0ef8ea8bf2a8f034b8ef2d5737038c75906dbaf6e9","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nc-class-c:lineage:55","source_registry_sha256":"e128656a3d00ba5437556728ebd87f5842c83601163739613417fe77cf9f423b","source_liveness_sha256":"dbfdf3e6d892a41c42c05809a9213d44a78aedd480dc6de23937c97292428b74"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Emergencies and crashes","heading":"C — Hitting an animal, brake failure, wet brakes, a stuck gas pedal, blowouts and flat tires, breakdowns, oncoming danger, running off the pavement, skids, crash avoidance and the duties after a crash (North Carolina)","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Hitting an animal, brake failure, wet brakes, a stuck gas pedal, blowouts and flat tires, breakdowns, oncoming danger, running off the pavement, skids, crash avoidance and the duties after a crash (North Carolina)
Knowledge domain: what to do after striking an animal, how to respond to mechanical emergencies (brake failure, wet brakes, a stuck gas pedal, blowouts, breakdowns), how to recover from running off the pavement and from skids, how to reduce harm when a crash is coming, and what North Carolina law requires of a driver after a crash.

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
After hitting an animal or finding an injured one, pull safely to the roadside, stay in the car with the doors locked and turn on the hazard lights. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Do not walk up to an animal you have struck, because it may be dangerous. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Report an animal collision to NC DOT at 1-877-368-4968 and to the nearest wildlife rehabilitator, who can check on the animal and any young nearby. [A01]
Why it matters: dynamic fact; phone number can change.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
In any emergency, the first rule is not to panic but to react quickly and correctly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
If the brakes fail in a manual car, shift to a lower gear, release the clutch and apply the emergency brake. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
If the brakes fail in an automatic car, apply the emergency brake and move the gear lever into the low range. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Using the emergency brake and low gear this way may damage them, but with failed brakes there is no better option. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
To dry wet brakes, drive a short distance while pressing lightly on the brake pedal so the friction heat evaporates the water. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
On a long or steep downhill, control speed with a lower gear rather than the brake pedal, shifting down at the top before you start down. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
If the gas pedal sticks, tap it or lift it with your foot, shift to neutral and brake firmly without locking the wheels, then get completely off the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A02
An unexplained bumpy ride is a reason to stop and check the tires; a blowout announces itself with a loud noise and a swerve. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A02
Before changing a flat, move fully off the road, set the parking brake and put out flares if you have them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A02
During a tire change, all passengers must get out on the passenger side and wait off the road, never standing in front of or behind the car. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
Turn on the flashers and parking lights and block the wheels so the car cannot roll while the tire is changed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
Never try to repair a car where it is exposed to passing traffic; call a tow truck or mechanic instead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
In a breakdown, move the car fully onto the shoulder, get everyone out on the passenger side and stand well away from the car, not in front of it or behind it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
To ask for help after a breakdown, tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood; after dark use the parking lights or flashers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Keep a flashlight or flares in the car at all times for emergencies. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
In a blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the car straight in your lane, then slow down by lifting off the accelerator. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
After a blowout, do not brake until the engine has slowed the car enough for you to keep control, then pull completely off the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F21 | anchor: A02
If an oncoming vehicle crosses the center line into your path, slow down at once and sound the horn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec13-F22 | anchor: A03
When a vehicle crosses into your lane, keep to the right, even if that means leaving the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F23 | anchor: A03
If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or jerk back toward the road, since you could skid or roll over. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F24 | anchor: A03
To recover from running onto the shoulder, ease off the gas, steer straight, let the engine slow the car, and return gradually only once traffic is clear and you are nearly stopped. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F25 | anchor: A03
Wet roads, ice and packed snow make skids more likely, so reduce speed gradually on them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F26 | anchor: A03
To avoid a skid with ABS, press the brake firmly and steadily without pumping; without ABS, pump the brakes gently. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F27 | anchor: A03
In a skid, ease off the gas and steer toward the direction the rear of the car is sliding. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F28 | anchor: A03
As the car begins to straighten out of a skid, turn the wheel back the other way so you do not over-steer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F29 | anchor: A03
If a crash seems likely, sound the horn, keep right and turn away from oncoming traffic, even into an open field off the road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F30 | anchor: A03
If you are about to be struck from behind with clear road ahead, accelerate away, be ready to brake if space runs out, brace yourself and press your head against the head rest. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F31 | anchor: A03
North Carolina law shields people who stop to help at a crash from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F32 | anchor: A03
If you are about to be hit, hold the steering wheel tightly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec13-F33 | anchor: A04
If a crash is about to happen, be ready to turn quickly to try to control the car, and as a last resort shield your face from breaking glass with your arms and hands. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F34 | anchor: A04
A driver involved in a crash must stop immediately; failing to stop breaks the law. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F35 | anchor: A04
At a crash scene, take steps to prevent further crashes, help the injured and make sure someone notifies law enforcement right away. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F36 | anchor: A04
If nobody is hurt or killed in a crash on a highway lane, ramp or shoulder, each car that can be driven safely should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F37 | anchor: A04
You must report a crash to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency right away if anyone is killed or injured or total property damage appears to be $1,000 or more. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F38 | anchor: A04
Not reporting a reportable crash can lead to prosecution and suspension of your driver license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F39 | anchor: A04
You should also report any crash to your insurance company, and in some cases you must file DMV forms proving liability insurance. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F40 | anchor: A04
After a crash you must give your name, address, license number, vehicle registration number and insurance company, and collect the same from the others involved. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec13-F41 | anchor: A04
If you cannot identify the other occupants or the owner of damaged property, write down everything you can and give it to the nearest law enforcement officer. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0080]

Misconceptions: braking hard during a blowout or after running onto the shoulder makes losing control more likely; in a skid you steer the way the rear is sliding, not the opposite way; anti-lock brakes should not be pumped, but brakes without ABS should be pumped gently; repairs on the edge of a travel lane are never safe; stopping to help at a crash is protected from civil liability unless the helper does intentional wrong or acts unruly; when no one is hurt, drivable cars should leave the travel lane rather than wait there.
Mnemonics: low gear and emergency brake when the pedal fails; grip, straight, off the gas for a blowout; steer where the back goes in a skid; stop, help, report, exchange after a crash.
Glossary: emergency brake means the separate parking brake used when the foot brake fails; low range means the lowest gear position on an automatic shifter; blowout means a sudden loss of air from a tire; over-steer means turning the wheel too far while recovering from a skid; reportable crash means one with death, injury or damage at or above the reporting threshold.
Dynamic facts: the NC DOT animal-collision phone number and the dollar threshold for a reportable crash can change and are flagged as dynamic.
